chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Yahya ibn Mu'ammar al-Attar, from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said during his illness in which he passed away: “Call my close friend for me.” So the two of them sent to their fathers. When Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله looked at them, he turned away from them. Then he said: “Call my close friend for me.” So a message was sent to Ali عليه السلام. When he looked at him, he bent closely over him, speaking to him.
When he came out, they met him and said to him, “What did your close friend tell you?” He said, “He narrated to me a thousand doors, each door opening a thousand doors.”

key_terms.أَعْرَضَ: he turned away, showing refusal toward those who were brought
key_terms.أَكَبَّ: he leaned closely over, indicating intimate and focused communication
key_terms.أَلْفَ بَابٍ: a thousand doors; a metaphor for vast branches of transmitted knowledge
key_terms.تُوُفِّيَ: he passed away; indicates the illness in which Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله died
key_terms.خَلِيلِي: my intimate friend; a term of special closeness used by Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.عَلِيٍّ: Ali عليه السلام, the one summoned by Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.مَرَضِهِ: his illness, referring to the final sickness before his passing

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله final private instruction to Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that during his final illness, Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله specifically requested his khalil, and when Ali عليه السلام was brought to him, he spoke with him privately. The report emphasizes the unique closeness of Ali عليه السلام to Rasul Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and indicates that he received extensive knowledge from him at that critical moment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Yahya Bin Moammar Al Attar, from Bashir Al Dahhan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said during his<sup>saww</sup> illness in which he<sup>saww</sup> passed away: ‘Call my<sup>saww</sup> friend for me<sup>saww</sup>’. So they both (Ayesha and Hafsa) sent a message to their fathers (Abu Bakr and Umar). So when Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> looked at them, turned away from them. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Call my<sup>saww</sup> friend for me<sup>saww</sup>’. So a message was sent to Ali<sup>asws</sup>. So when he<sup>saww</sup> looked at him<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>saww</sup> got engrossed (engaged) upon it narrating to him<sup>asws</sup>.

So when he<sup>asws</sup> came out, they (Abu Bakr and Umar) met him<sup>asws</sup> and they both said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What did your<sup>asws</sup> friend narrate to you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>saww</sup> narrated to me<sup>asws</sup> a thousand topics, with each topic opening a thousand topics’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Salih ibn al-Sindi from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Yahya ibn Ma‘mar al-‘Attar from Bashir al-Dahhan from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“the Messenger of Allah during the illness from which died said, ‘Call my beloved one to come to me.” We sent to call the fathers of the two of them (‘A’isha and hafsa’s fathers). When the Messenger of Allah looked at them he turned away from them. He them said again, “Call my beloved one to come to me.” Ali was then called. When the Messenger of Allah looked at him, he became engrossed talking to him.
When Ali left the two met him and asked, “What did your beloved say to you?” He (Ali) replied, “He narrated to me a thousand chapter from each of which a thousand chapter opens.”
